digest.component_or_area: inbound reconciliation: fetcher, differ, apply layers for parent field
problem_keywords: parent_id remains set after jira removal
data loss on cleared parent edge
managed refs cannot prove peer state
propositions: When a parent is removed in Jira, the local parent_id field remains set because the fetcher omits the absent parent from the snapshot and the differ refuses to emit parent_id=None

The snapshot parent field is left absent when queried and found None, making it indistinguishable from an unqueried or failed read, so the differ cannot safely emit a clear without risking spurious deletion of locally-set parents

The differ collapses three states into one None return (genuinely absent parent, unresolved parent key, failed/truncated read) and refuses to emit any clear, preserving the original guard's intent but preventing legitimate clears on observed-parentless cases

The managed-refs guard alone cannot prevent data loss because add_managed_ref only proves local origin, never that the peer ever had the parent; the same-pass outbound suppression cannot fire because parent writes are never emitted for non-epic children

Change 1288 merged and the production Cloud bridge destroyed 63 parent edges by clearing parents on tickets whose local parents were never pushed to the peer, proving the detection approach is fundamentally unsafe without peer-state baseline evidence
